gre-readiness-check-verbal-045.prompt: The restorer’s note on the gilt frame was unexpectedly ______: it skipped ornamental trivia and named only the joints likely to split if the painting traveled.

options.a: pragmatic
options.b: ornamental
options.c: nostalgic
options.d: encyclopedic

gre-readiness-check-verbal-045.explanation: The colon explains the blank: the note ignored decorative detail and listed only travel risks. That is a practical, risk-first report, so pragmatic fits. Encyclopedic would pile on trivia; ornamental and nostalgic describe tone or décor, not the selective triage.

distractorExplanations.b: Ornamental would dwell on gilt décor, which is exactly the trivia the note skipped.
distractorExplanations.c: Nostalgic names a sentimental tone; the sentence is about selective, risk-based reporting.
distractorExplanations.d: Encyclopedic means covering everything; the note is praised for leaving most details out.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-046.prompt: Far from being ______, the lab memo ______ every unverified claim and left only measurements another bench could rerun.

options.a: credulous … repeated
options.b: gullible … excised
options.c: cryptic … invented
options.d: lavish … padded

gre-readiness-check-verbal-046.explanation: “Far from being” signals a contrast with sloppy belief. The memo cut unverified claims and kept rerunnable numbers, so it was not gullible and it excised weak claims. Repeated or padded would keep extra text; invented contradicts leaving only measurements.

distractorExplanations.a: A credulous memo would keep dubious claims, not strip them; repeated is the opposite of cutting.
distractorExplanations.c: Invented claims would not leave only rerunnable measurements; cryptic also misses the purge.
distractorExplanations.d: Lavish padding adds unverified material; the memo is described as cutting it away.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-047.prompt: Sphagnum peat can hold a leather shoe for centuries because the bog is cold, acidic, and nearly oxygen-free; bacteria that normally chew collagen stall. When a drainage ditch lets air in, the same shoe can crumble in a few seasons. Conservators therefore treat a newly drained find as a race against oxidation, not as a relic already “pickled for good.” The passage most strongly supports which claim?

options.a: Peat always mineralizes collagen faster than dry desert sand does.
options.b: Drainage ditches were dug mainly to recover shoes for museums.
options.c: Anoxia, not mere wetness, is what keeps bog leather intact.
options.d: Once a shoe is lifted, oxidation can no longer harm the collagen.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-047.explanation: The author ties preservation to cold, acid, and lack of oxygen, then shows air after drainage destroying the leather. Wetness alone is not the mechanism; anoxia is. The other choices invent desert comparisons, ditch motives, or a false safety after lifting.

distractorExplanations.a: No desert comparison appears; the contrast is bog anoxia versus later air, not sand.
distractorExplanations.b: The ditch is a threat to preservation, not a recovery plan for museum shoes.
distractorExplanations.d: Lifting into air is exactly when oxidation becomes an urgent conservation race.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-048.prompt: In the epidemiologist’s press note, “we must qualify the drop in cases” uses qualify most nearly to mean

options.a: certify the numbers as courtroom-ready facts
options.b: celebrate the drop as a finished public victory
options.c: replace the dataset with a smaller convenience sample
options.d: limit the claim with caveats about who was counted

gre-readiness-check-verbal-048.explanation: In academic English, to qualify a claim is to restrict it, not to license it. The epidemiologist is hedging who was counted, so the drop is not a blunt headline. Certify and celebrate ignore the caution; replacing the dataset is a method change the sentence does not make.

distractorExplanations.a: Qualify here is not a legal stamp of truth; it is a hedge on scope.
distractorExplanations.b: Celebrating a victory would drop the caution the verb is there to add.
distractorExplanations.c: Swapping in a convenience sample is a design change, not what qualify means.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-049.prompt: On a northern ferry route, captains still file “ice letters” even though satellite maps show the channel. The letters record which leads opened overnight, which ridges would scrape a hull, and which buoys vanished under wind-packed slush. Dispatchers treat the letters as a lagging, human overlay on the satellite feed, not as a substitute for it. The author’s primary point is that the letters

options.a: add local, time-sensitive hull risks satellites can miss
options.b: have made satellite ice charts legally obsolete overnight
options.c: exist mainly to entertain passengers with polar folklore
options.d: prove that buoys are more accurate than any human report

gre-readiness-check-verbal-049.explanation: The details—overnight leads, hull-scraping ridges, buried buoys—are local hazards, and dispatchers use the letters as an overlay, not a replacement. That supports adding time-sensitive risk the maps miss. Obsolete satellites, folklore, and buoy supremacy contradict the overlay claim.

distractorExplanations.b: Dispatchers explicitly do not treat letters as a substitute for the satellite feed.
distractorExplanations.c: The letters are operational hull notes, not passenger entertainment.
distractorExplanations.d: Buoys vanish under slush; the letters exist because hardware can disappear.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-050.prompt: When the curator calls the collector’s taste “catholic,” she most nearly means that the collector

options.a: bought only liturgical objects from one diocese
options.b: gathered widely, with few stylistic taboos
options.c: refused any work made after 1900
options.d: preferred unsigned sketches to finished canvases

gre-readiness-check-verbal-050.explanation: Lowercase catholic means wide-ranging, not confessional. Few taboos matches a broad collection. A diocesan buying rule, a 1900 cutoff, or a sketch-only habit would narrow taste, the opposite of the word in this museum usage.

distractorExplanations.a: Liturgical-only buying is sectarian, not catholic in the “broad taste” sense.
distractorExplanations.c: A hard date cutoff is a restriction; catholic taste is the opposite of a taboo.
distractorExplanations.d: Preferring sketches is a narrow preference, not wide-ranging collecting.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-051.prompt: Early cinema intertitles were often ______, because projectionists needed a card short enough to read aloud yet ______ enough to carry a plot turn.

options.a: verbose … cryptic
options.b: ornate … trivial
options.c: terse … lucid
options.d: muddled … ornate

gre-readiness-check-verbal-051.explanation: The constraint is read-aloud brevity plus a plot-carrying message, so terse and lucid pair. Verbose fights shortness; cryptic or muddled would hide the plot turn; trivial would not carry it.

distractorExplanations.a: Verbose cards are not short enough to read aloud; cryptic hides the plot turn.
distractorExplanations.b: Ornate length and trivial content both fail the need to carry a plot beat.
distractorExplanations.d: Muddled wording and ornate extra words work against a clear, short card.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-052.prompt: A city’s new sorting code grouped streets by truck loop, not by neighborhood name. Residents complained that “their” district had vanished from the label, yet mis-sorted parcels fell by a third. The postal engineer’s brief reply was that a code can be socially illegible and still be logistically kind. Which inference is best supported?

options.a: Neighborhood names are useless for any civic purpose.
options.b: Residents invented the drop in mis-sorts to win the debate.
options.c: Truck loops were drawn to erase minority district names.
options.d: A label can offend local identity while improving delivery.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-052.explanation: The facts are identity complaint plus fewer mis-sorts, and the engineer says a code can be socially opaque yet logistically helpful. That is exactly offense to identity with better delivery. The other options leap to civic uselessness, fraud, or a motive the passage never states.

distractorExplanations.a: The passage never says neighborhood names fail every civic use; only this label changed.
distractorExplanations.b: The drop in mis-sorts is presented as a result, not a resident fabrication.
distractorExplanations.c: No evidence is given that loops were a scheme to erase minority names.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-053.prompt: Critics called the mayor’s apology “anodyne.” In that review, anodyne most nearly means

options.a: soothingly vague, with little concrete amends
options.b: brutally specific about every failed vote
options.c: written in a foreign legal jargon on purpose
options.d: delivered too late to appear on any broadcast

gre-readiness-check-verbal-053.explanation: Anodyne means soothing and inoffensive, often by being bland. “Soothingly vague, little amends” captures the critical jab. Brutal specificity, foreign jargon, and lateness are different charges the word does not carry.

distractorExplanations.b: Brutal specificity is the opposite of an anodyne, pain-dulling statement.
distractorExplanations.c: Legal jargon is a register complaint, not what anodyne denotes.
distractorExplanations.d: Timing on a broadcast is unrelated to the word’s “blandly soothing” sense.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-054.prompt: Andean khipu cords encode information in knot type, cord color, and pendant position. Spanish notaries sometimes treated them as mere mnemonic tassels, yet colonial lawsuits show Indigenous litigants introducing khipu as accounts of herds and labor. The author’s contrast most nearly suggests that khipu were

options.a: decorative tassels with no administrative use
options.b: records outsiders could mistake for ornaments
options.c: alphabetic books copied from Spanish ledgers
options.d: only used after independence as folk crafts

gre-readiness-check-verbal-054.explanation: Knot, color, and position are a recording system; notaries misread them as tassels while lawsuits used them as accounts. That is outsider misrecognition, not proof they were empty décor, alphabetic books, or post-independence crafts.

distractorExplanations.a: Lawsuits using khipu as herd and labor accounts contradict “no administrative use.”
distractorExplanations.c: The passage describes knots and colors, not copied alphabetic ledgers.
distractorExplanations.d: Colonial lawsuits place khipu in the Spanish period, not only after independence.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-055.prompt: The archaeologist argued that the stone basin was a tidal mill, not a fish trap: the sluice stones were ______ for holding a millpond, and the floor was ______ with grit from grinding, not with fishbone.

options.a: too fragile … littered
options.b: too narrow … gilded
options.c: well suited … scored
options.d: badly sealed … painted

gre-readiness-check-verbal-055.explanation: A millpond needs a basin that can hold water, and a mill floor should show grinding grit, so well suited and scored fit. Fragile, narrow, or badly sealed sluices fight a millpond; gilded, painted, or fishbone-heavy floors fight the grinding evidence.

distractorExplanations.a: Fragile sluices would not hold a millpond; littered also fails the grit contrast.
distractorExplanations.b: Narrow sluices and a gilded floor do not support a working mill reading.
distractorExplanations.d: Badly sealed stones leak a pond; paint is not grinding evidence.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-056.prompt: The diarist called the gallery crowd “restive” before the delayed opening. Restive most nearly means

options.a: quietly scholarly and eager to take notes
options.b: already leaving because the art disappointed
options.c: asleep on benches after a long journey
options.d: impatient and hard to keep standing still

gre-readiness-check-verbal-056.explanation: Restive describes people impatient under delay, fidgeting rather than calm. A delayed opening supplies the wait. Scholarly quiet, departure after seeing art, and sleep miss that restless-waiting sense.

distractorExplanations.a: Quiet note-taking is composed; restive people are unsettled, not scholarly-calm.
distractorExplanations.b: They have not yet entered; disappointment with the art cannot explain the wait.
distractorExplanations.c: Sleep is inertia; restive implies irritated movement under constraint.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-057.prompt: English common-law pleadings once mixed English with Law French, a courtroom dialect that kept words like voir dire long after Parisian French had moved on. Reformers later mocked the mix as snobbery, but clerks defended it as a precision tool: a term of art that stopped a lay synonym from smuggling in the wrong duty. The passage indicates that clerks valued Law French mainly as

options.a: a way to pin legal duties to set terms of art
options.b: proof that Paris still governed English courts
options.c: a fashion that made pleadings more poetic
options.d: a code designed so jurors could never understand a trial

gre-readiness-check-verbal-057.explanation: Clerks’ defense is precision: a term of art blocking a sloppy synonym. That is pinning duties to set words. Parisian governance, poetry, and a plot to baffle jurors are not what the clerks say.

distractorExplanations.b: The dialect had already diverged from Paris; that is not the clerks’ defense.
distractorExplanations.c: Clerks argue technical precision, not poetic fashion.
distractorExplanations.d: The aim stated is stopping wrong duties, not hiding the whole trial from jurors.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-058.prompt: Biologists treating a whale “song” as a dialect must be ______: a pattern that sounds new may be ______ of an old theme shifted up a few notes, not a separate language.

options.a: dogmatic … a proof
options.b: cautious … variant
options.c: exultant … a fossil
options.d: dismissive … a hoax

gre-readiness-check-verbal-058.explanation: The warning is not to over-split languages: a “new” pattern may be an old theme transposed. Cautious plus variant matches. Dogmatic proof, fossils, and hoaxes do not capture transposition of a known theme.

distractorExplanations.a: Dogmatic proof of a new language is what the sentence tells biologists to avoid.
distractorExplanations.c: Exultant and fossil miss the idea of a shifted, still-living theme.
distractorExplanations.d: A hoax would be fake; the worry is misclassifying a real variant.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-059.prompt: The manuscript historian wrote that later varnish “occluded” the underdrawing. Occluded most nearly means

options.a: cleaned until the charcoal lines shone
options.b: dated the drawing to a later century
options.c: blocked the lines from ordinary view
options.d: proved the varnish was original to the shop

gre-readiness-check-verbal-059.explanation: To occlude is to shut off or hide. Varnish covering an underdrawing blocks those lines from view. Cleaning, dating, and proving originality are other conservation claims, not the verb’s sense.

distractorExplanations.a: Cleaning would reveal lines; occlude is covering, not polishing them.
distractorExplanations.b: Occlude is not a dating verb; it describes visual blockage.
distractorExplanations.d: Whether varnish is original is a separate authenticity question.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-060.prompt: A city that pays census enumerators by completed forms will undercount crowded houses: a worker can finish faster by skipping a walk-up with many names. Paying by address visit, with a bonus only after supervisors match names to utility meters, slowed the count but raised the share of multi-family buildings found. The example is meant to show that

options.a: utility meters are treated as a perfect census substitute
options.b: enumerators refuse any bonus on principle as a matter of ethics
options.c: speed always produces a more complete city count in practice
options.d: pay rules can hide the households that are hardest to list

gre-readiness-check-verbal-060.explanation: Piecework by form rewards skipping hard walk-ups; visit-plus-meter checks slow work but find more multi-family houses. The point is incentive design hiding hard-to-list households. Perfect meters, principled bonus refusal, and speed-as-completeness are not supported.

distractorExplanations.a: Meters are a supervisory check, not a claimed full substitute for enumeration.
distractorExplanations.b: The passage discusses payment design, not a moral strike against bonuses.
distractorExplanations.c: The faster rule is the one that missed crowded houses.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-061.prompt: The typefounder’s specimen sheet was ______ rather than luxurious: it showed the same alphabet in sizes a newspaper could actually ______.

options.a: useful … buy
options.b: baroque … hoard
options.c: cryptic … melt
options.d: lavish … hide

gre-readiness-check-verbal-061.explanation: A sheet aimed at newspaper purchase, not luxury display, is useful, and buy completes the commercial use. Baroque/lavish and hoard/hide/melt fight a practical specimen for sale.

distractorExplanations.b: Baroque luxury and hoarding contradict a working newspaper specimen.
distractorExplanations.c: A cryptic sheet you melt is not a sales sample of usable sizes.
distractorExplanations.d: Lavish hiding is the opposite of showing buyable newspaper sizes.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-062.prompt: In the broker’s diary, a “precipitous” slide in the tin price most nearly means the drop was

options.a: gentle and spread across several quiet years
options.b: steep and sudden, with little warning
options.c: caused only by a clerical rounding error
options.d: confined to one warehouse that never sold tin

gre-readiness-check-verbal-062.explanation: Precipitous means extremely steep, like a cliff. For a price, that is a sudden, sharp fall. Gentle years, a mere rounding glitch, and a warehouse that never sold tin do not match the ordinary figurative use.

distractorExplanations.a: Gentle, multi-year easing is the antonym of a precipitous drop.
distractorExplanations.c: A rounding error is a cause guess; the adjective describes speed and slope.
distractorExplanations.d: A non-selling warehouse is unrelated to a market-wide price slide.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-063.prompt: East Asian lacquer objects are built in dozens of thin coats that cure slowly. A later repairer who slaps on a thick modern varnish may make the piece look even, but the new skin traps moisture and then peels, taking original layers with it. Museum labs therefore prefer reversible, thin fills even when the surface still looks slightly hungry. The lab policy is best explained as

options.a: a preference for shiny varnish over all historic coatings
options.b: proof that thick coats always cure faster than thin ones
options.c: protect original layers even if the repair looks hungrier
options.d: a ban on showing any lacquer object that is not perfect

gre-readiness-check-verbal-063.explanation: Thick modern skins look even but then peel original coats; thin reversible fills look hungrier but spare the object. That is conservation over sleekness. Shiny-first, faster thick cure, and a display ban are not the stated policy.

distractorExplanations.a: The lab rejects thick modern varnish precisely because it harms historic coats.
distractorExplanations.b: The passage never claims thick coats cure faster; it warns they trap moisture.
distractorExplanations.d: Hungry-looking fills are accepted; display is not banned for imperfect surfaces.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-064.prompt: Dendrochronology can ______ a timber only if the ring series is long enough to ______ against a regional master chart; a short fragment stays mute.

options.a: date … clash
options.b: burn … rhyme
options.c: carve … vanish
options.d: place … match

gre-readiness-check-verbal-064.explanation: The method dates (places in time) a timber by matching rings to a master series; a short piece cannot lock. Clash, burn, carve, vanish, and rhyme do not describe that comparison.

distractorExplanations.a: Clash against a master chart would prevent a date, not enable one.
distractorExplanations.b: Burning timber and rhyming rings are not how a chronology is built.
distractorExplanations.c: Carving that vanishes is unrelated to comparing ring series.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-065.prompt: The wall text called the ferry terminal a “liminal” hall. Liminal most nearly means

options.a: a threshold space, not a destination
options.b: permanently residential, like a small hotel
options.c: windowless and therefore legally a bunker
options.d: reserved for ceremonies of a single faith

gre-readiness-check-verbal-065.explanation: Liminal means on a threshold, betwixt and between. A ferry hall people pass through fits. Residential hotel, bunker law, and single-faith rites are different spatial claims.

distractorExplanations.b: A hotel stay is a destination of sorts; liminal spaces are passages.
distractorExplanations.c: Liminal is not a building-code claim about windows or bunkers.
distractorExplanations.d: The word is not a sectarian reservation; it names a threshold state.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-066.prompt: Quarry ledgers listed blocks by grain direction, not just by cubic feet, because a beam set against the grain can snap under a load a same-size block would carry if the grain ran with the span. When a later contractor priced only volume, several lintels failed. The author’s example warns that

options.a: cubic feet are never useful in any stone contract at all
options.b: grain can make equal volumes differ in strength
options.c: lintels fail only when masons refuse to use any metal
options.d: quarry ledgers were written only to confuse later buyers

gre-readiness-check-verbal-066.explanation: Same volume, different grain, different load: pricing volume alone produced failed lintels. That is unequal strength under a volume-only price. “Never useful,” metal-only failure, and a conspiracy to confuse are extra.

distractorExplanations.a: Volume still matters; the warning is using volume without grain.
distractorExplanations.c: The failures are tied to grain vs. span, not to a ban on metal.
distractorExplanations.d: Ledgers listed grain to inform, not to puzzle later contractors.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-067.prompt: Railway telegraph codes grew ______ because each extra word cost money, yet they had to remain ______ enough that a tired night clerk would not send a train onto the wrong siding.

options.a: florid … quite ambiguous
options.b: chatty … ornamental
options.c: compact … unambiguous
options.d: poetic … rather cryptic

gre-readiness-check-verbal-067.explanation: Cost per word pushes compression; safety for a tired clerk demands unambiguity. Florid, chatty, poetic, ambiguous, ornamental, and cryptic all fight one of those two constraints.

distractorExplanations.a: Florid extra words cost money; ambiguous wording is what the clerk must not face.
distractorExplanations.b: Chatty and ornamental messages would balloon the per-word bill.
distractorExplanations.d: Poetic cryptic phrasing is the opposite of a safe night-clerk code.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-068.prompt: Colleagues found the hydrologist’s forecast “sanguine.” In that complaint, sanguine most nearly means

options.a: gory, obsessed with listing flood casualties
options.b: written in blood-red ink for extra emphasis
options.c: neutral, refusing any water-level prediction at all
options.d: too cheerful about a mild coming season

gre-readiness-check-verbal-068.explanation: Sanguine as a temperament word means confidently optimistic. A complaint about a forecast that is too cheerful matches. Gory, red ink, and refusal to predict are traps from blood imagery or from “no forecast.”

distractorExplanations.a: The blood sense of sanguine is not the complaint about a mild-season forecast.
distractorExplanations.b: Ink color is literalist and unrelated to the colleagues’ charge.
distractorExplanations.c: A sanguine forecast is a prediction, not a refusal to predict.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-069.prompt: A school atlas that uses a Mercator world map makes Greenland look like a peer of Africa. The cartographer’s footnote does not scold children for “believing maps”; it notes that a projection chosen to keep compass rhumb lines straight will inflate high latitudes. The footnote’s purpose is to

options.a: link the distortion to a navigational choice
options.b: prove that all school atlases should abandon paper maps
options.c: argue that Greenland is in fact larger than Africa today
options.d: blame students for misreading every kind of chart they see

gre-readiness-check-verbal-069.explanation: The footnote links inflated polar land to keeping rhumb lines straight. That is cause (navigation design) for the look. It does not dump paper maps, reverse geography, or scold every misreading.

distractorExplanations.b: Nothing is said about abandoning paper atlases.
distractorExplanations.c: The point is apparent size, not a claim that Greenland truly outranks Africa.
distractorExplanations.d: The author explicitly does not scold children for believing maps.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-070.prompt: The dyer’s log was ______ about recipes yet ______ about gossip: it listed alum weights to the ounce and never named which household had commissioned the cloth.

options.a: vague … lavish
options.b: exact … silent
options.c: playful … loud
options.d: sloppy … candid

gre-readiness-check-verbal-070.explanation: Ounce-level alum weights are exact; never naming the client is silence about gossip. Vague/sloppy fight the weights; lavish/loud/candid fight the refusal to name households.

distractorExplanations.a: Vague recipes contradict ounce-level alum weights.
distractorExplanations.c: Playful loud gossip is the opposite of a log that never names clients.
distractorExplanations.d: Sloppy and candid invert both halves: precision on recipes, silence on people.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-071.prompt: The field team labeled the soil map “provisional.” Provisional most nearly means

options.a: permanently adopted as the county’s legal plat
options.b: secret, withheld from every neighboring lab
options.c: temporary, open to revision with more cores
options.d: decorative, meant only for a gallery wall

gre-readiness-check-verbal-071.explanation: Provisional means adopted for now, subject to change. More cores implying revision matches. Legal permanence, secrecy, and gallery décor do not.

distractorExplanations.a: A legal plat is settled; provisional flags the opposite status.
distractorExplanations.b: The word does not mean classified or withheld from peers.
distractorExplanations.d: A working soil map is not a gallery decoration.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-072.prompt: A cheap adhesive binding can look tidy on day one and then drop leaves after a dry winter, because the glue shrinks and the text block was never sewn through the folds. A sewn binding may open less “flat” in a display case, yet the folds still hold when glue fails. Conservators therefore treat flop-open display as a poor proxy for a sound book. The passage suggests that

options.a: all glue is forbidden in any conservation lab on principle
options.b: display-case flatness is the best test of a sound binding
options.c: winter dryness never affects adhesive books in storage
options.d: sewn folds can outlast a glued-only spine

gre-readiness-check-verbal-072.explanation: Glue-only books shed leaves when glue shrinks; sewn folds still hold. Flat opening is called a bad proxy. That supports sewing outlasting a glued spine, not a total glue ban or flatness-as-best-test.

distractorExplanations.a: The critique is glue-only cheap bindings, not a ban on every adhesive.
distractorExplanations.b: Flat opening is explicitly a poor proxy for soundness.
distractorExplanations.c: A dry winter is the example of when glue shrinks and leaves drop.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-073.prompt: The tea taster’s sheet looked ______ to outsiders, but each hooked mark was a ______ for a known fault—smoke, staleness, or a wet-store must—not a doodle.

options.a: coded … shorthand
options.b: lyrical … a novel
options.c: blank … a sermon
options.d: ornate … a joke

gre-readiness-check-verbal-073.explanation: Outsiders cannot read the marks, yet each stands for a listed fault, so cryptic shorthand. Novel, sermon, joke, lyrical, blank, and ornate miss that coded, professional compression.

distractorExplanations.b: A novel lyrical mark would be new writing, not a code for known faults.
distractorExplanations.c: The sheet is marked, not blank, and a sermon is not a fault code.
distractorExplanations.d: Ornate jokes would not map hooked marks onto smoke and must.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-074.prompt: Reviewers called the opening chord “arresting.” Arresting most nearly means

options.a: legally detaining the composer after the concert
options.b: so striking that listeners stopped to attend
options.c: so quiet that the hall drifted into sleep
options.d: so conventional that nobody noticed the start

gre-readiness-check-verbal-074.explanation: Arresting as praise means holding attention, striking. Legal detention is a pun; sleep and conventional invisibility are opposites of that force.

distractorExplanations.a: The concert-review sense is not a police action against the composer.
distractorExplanations.c: Sleep is lost attention; arresting music seizes it.
distractorExplanations.d: Unnoticed convention is the opposite of a striking opening.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-075.prompt: In Javanese wayang, the dalang speaks many voices from one throat while the lamp throws puppets as shadows. Visitors who treat the show as “just silhouettes” miss that the moral argument lives in the dalang’s timing—when a clown figure is allowed to puncture a king’s speech. The author implies that meaning in wayang is

options.a: located only in the painted leather, never in speech
options.b: lost unless the audience reads a printed libretto first
options.c: carried as much by voiced timing as by the shadows
options.d: intended solely as children’s entertainment after harvest

gre-readiness-check-verbal-075.explanation: The warning is that silhouettes-alone miss the dalang’s timed interruptions, so meaning rides voice and timing with the shadows. Leather-only, libretto-required, and harvest-kids-only are not claimed.

distractorExplanations.a: Speech and timing are exactly what visitors miss if they watch only silhouettes.
distractorExplanations.b: No printed libretto is required in the account given.
distractorExplanations.d: A moral argument via a clown puncturing a king is not framed as kids-only harvest fun.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-076.prompt: The etcher’s bite was ______: too little acid and the line stayed ______; too much and the plate would undercut, collapsing fine hatch.

options.a: irrelevant … gilded
options.b: random … musical
options.c: ceremonial … blank
options.d: exacting … faint

gre-readiness-check-verbal-076.explanation: The process sits between too little acid (faint line) and too much (undercut hatch), so the bite is exacting. Irrelevant, random, ceremonial, gilded, musical, and blank do not name that tight window.

distractorExplanations.a: Bite time is not irrelevant, and gilding is not the weak-line problem.
distractorExplanations.b: Random musical lines ignore the acid-window craft described.
distractorExplanations.c: Ceremonial blankness is not a description of controlled acid bite.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-077.prompt: The engineer claimed a new culvert would “obviate” the annual sandbag line. Obviate most nearly means

options.a: make the sandbag ritual unnecessary
options.b: make the floodwaters legally obligatory
options.c: paint the sandbags a more visible color
options.d: move the sandbag storage to a farther barn

gre-readiness-check-verbal-077.explanation: To obviate is to prevent a need from arising. A culvert that removes the yearly sandbag duty matches. Legal obligation, paint, and storage moves are unrelated verbs.

distractorExplanations.b: Obviate does not mean to require floods by law.
distractorExplanations.c: Repainting bags still assumes the ritual continues.
distractorExplanations.d: Relocating storage does not remove the need for the line.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-078.prompt: A harbor that dredges only the shipping channel can still shoal at the ferry dock, because wakes remix silt sideways into the berth. Charts that show a deep centerline therefore comfort captains until the ferry scrapes at low tide. The author’s caution is that

options.a: all dredging is wasted money in every harbor
options.b: a deep channel chart can hide a shallow berth
options.c: ferry wakes never move silt once a channel is cut
options.d: low tide is irrelevant if the centerline is deep

gre-readiness-check-verbal-078.explanation: Sideways wake remix fills the dock while the channel looks deep; the scrape at low tide is the punch. That is a misleading centerline chart. Universal waste, immobile silt, and tide irrelevance contradict the example.

distractorExplanations.a: The issue is incomplete dredging of the berth, not that all dredging is waste.
distractorExplanations.c: Wakes remixing silt into the berth is the mechanism given.
distractorExplanations.d: Low tide is when the ferry scrapes, so tide is not irrelevant.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-079.prompt: Makers who ______ a violin with a thick modern plastic coat may seal the wood against sweat, yet they also ______ the instrument’s ability to age in the slow, breathable way older varnishes allowed.

options.a: starve … enhance
options.b: stain … celebrate
options.c: encase … blunt
options.d: ignore … restore

gre-readiness-check-verbal-079.explanation: A thick plastic coat encases wood and blunts breathable aging. Starve/ignore do not describe coating; enhance/celebrate/restore contradict loss of that aging.

distractorExplanations.a: A thick coat does not starve the wood of finish, and it does not enhance old-style aging.
distractorExplanations.b: Stain-and-celebrate misses both the plastic skin and the lost breathability.
distractorExplanations.d: They are not ignoring the violin, nor restoring older aging, by adding plastic.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-080.prompt: Students called the footnote “recondite.” Recondite most nearly means

options.a: aimed at beginners with no prior reading at all
options.b: copied word-for-word from a popular public blog
options.c: concerned only with dining-hall gossip and jokes
options.d: obscure and hard for outsiders to enter

gre-readiness-check-verbal-080.explanation: Recondite means obscure, known to few. A hard footnote matches. Beginner-friendly, blog-popular, and dining gossip are the wrong social range.

distractorExplanations.a: Beginner-aimed notes are accessible, not recondite.
distractorExplanations.b: A popular blog copy would be widely known, the opposite charge.
distractorExplanations.c: Dining gossip is trivial chatter, not dense specialist obscurity.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-081.prompt: Drillers’ well logs look like dull columns of sand and clay, but a hydrologist reads them as a story of buried riverbeds: a coarse sand streak may be an old channel that still carries water sideways. Towns that permit wells by lot size alone, ignoring those streaks, can dry a neighbor’s shallow well. The hydrologist’s implicit recommendation is to

options.a: read buried channels when granting well permits
options.b: ban all new wells no matter what the log shows
options.c: treat every sand streak as oil rather than water
options.d: issue permits only by surface lot size, as now

gre-readiness-check-verbal-081.explanation: Lot-size-only permits ignore buried channels that steal a neighbor’s water; logs should inform permits. A total ban, oil misread, and keeping lot-size-only policy fight that implication.

distractorExplanations.b: The critique is how wells are sited, not a call to ban wells entirely.
distractorExplanations.c: The sand streak is framed as a water-bearing old channel, not an oil play.
distractorExplanations.d: Lot-size-only permitting is the practice blamed for drying neighbors.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-082.prompt: A coppiced woodland looks ______ to a visitor expecting old trunks, yet the repeated cutting is ______: it keeps stools alive and yields poles on a known cycle.

options.a: primeval … accidental
options.b: mangled … deliberate
options.c: ornamental … illegal
options.d: barren … mythical

gre-readiness-check-verbal-082.explanation: Cut stools look damaged, but the system is intentional management. Primeval, accidental, illegal, mythical, ornamental, and barren miss that managed-yield reading.

distractorExplanations.a: Primeval accident is the opposite of a known cutting cycle.
distractorExplanations.c: Coppice is a working system, not merely ornamental or illegal.
distractorExplanations.d: Yielding poles on a cycle is not barren, and it is not mythical.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-083.prompt: The archivist called the merchant’s cipher “inscrutable” until the key turned up in a lining. Inscrutable most nearly means

options.a: already fully decoded by every clerk in the office
options.b: written in a huge, childish print on purpose
options.c: impossible to interpret without a key
options.d: too dull to be worth storing in the archive

gre-readiness-check-verbal-083.explanation: Inscrutable means not readable; the lining key ending that state confirms a locked cipher. Already decoded, childish print, and boring storage are other complaints.

distractorExplanations.a: If every clerk had decoded it, the key in the lining would not matter.
distractorExplanations.b: Letter size is not what inscrutable describes.
distractorExplanations.d: Worth-storing is a value judgment, not unreadability.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-084.prompt: The estate icehouse was ______ in summer not because magic chilled the stone, but because thick walls and a drained floor ______ meltwater before it could soak the stored blocks.

options.a: useless … invited
options.b: tropical … painted
options.c: noisy … boiled
options.d: cold … shed

gre-readiness-check-verbal-084.explanation: The icehouse stayed cold because meltwater was shed, not soaked back into the ice. Useless/tropical/noisy and invited/painted/boiled invert the engineering.

distractorExplanations.a: A working icehouse is not useless, and inviting meltwater would warm the ice.
distractorExplanations.b: Tropical painted walls do not explain stored blocks staying frozen.
distractorExplanations.c: Boiling meltwater is the opposite of draining it away from the ice.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-085.prompt: Jacquard punched cards did not “think,” but they did let a loom repeat a portrait without a weaver memorizing every weft. Factory critics who called the cards a theft of skill were answering a real change: pattern memory moved from a person’s head onto a stack of holes. The author’s best paraphrase is that the cards

options.a: moved a pattern that once lived in the weaver
options.b: proved looms had become fully conscious machines
options.c: had no effect on whose memory the pattern required
options.d: existed only as a metaphor, never as shop-floor tools

gre-readiness-check-verbal-085.explanation: Pattern memory moving from head to punched holes is externalization. Consciousness, no change, and metaphor-only contradict the factory description.

distractorExplanations.b: The opening denies that the cards think or that the loom is conscious.
distractorExplanations.c: The whole point is a real shift in where pattern memory sits.
distractorExplanations.d: They are described as shop-floor stacks of holes, not mere metaphors.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-086.prompt: The editor praised the obituary as “spare.” Spare most nearly means

options.a: padded with every distant cousin’s nickname
options.b: lean, with no extra ornamental clauses
options.c: written to spare the printer unused ink
options.d: so cruel that relatives asked for a rewrite

gre-readiness-check-verbal-086.explanation: Spare prose is lean, without ornament. Padding, a joke about ink, and cruelty (a different sense of spare/sparing) miss the stylistic praise.

distractorExplanations.a: Padding with nicknames is the opposite of spare writing.
distractorExplanations.c: Printers’ ink is a pun, not the editor’s stylistic sense.
distractorExplanations.d: Cruelty would not usually be praised; spare here is lean, not vicious.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-087.prompt: Coastal salt pans look empty, but their geometry is a clock: shallow ponds evaporate in sequence, and workers move brine only when a crust begins. A tourist photo that crops to “white desert” therefore erases labor timing. Which statement best captures the author’s concern?

options.a: Salt pans cannot produce salt without imported rock salt.
options.b: Geometry of ponds is irrelevant to when brine is moved.
options.c: A pretty crop can hide the labor that makes salt.
options.d: Tourists should be banned from all coastal industries.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-087.explanation: Sequential ponds plus timed moving of brine are labor; the cropped “white desert” photo erases that clock. Import rock salt, irrelevant geometry, and a tourist ban are not the concern.

distractorExplanations.a: The process described is evaporation of brine, not importing rock salt.
distractorExplanations.b: Pond geometry is presented as the clock that times the work.
distractorExplanations.d: The target is a misleading crop, not a ban on visitors.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-088.prompt: A court interpreter must be ______ rather than eloquent: adding a graceful extra clause can ______ a witness’s actual, halting words.

options.a: theatrical … honor
options.b: florid … clarify
options.c: inventive … preserve
options.d: literal … distort

gre-readiness-check-verbal-088.explanation: The job is fidelity, not speechmaking; extra grace distorts a halting witness. Theatrical/florid/inventive plus honor/clarify/preserve invert the ethics.

distractorExplanations.a: Theatrical additions do not honor a witness’s actual wording.
distractorExplanations.b: Florid extra clauses are what risk changing, not clarifying, the record.
distractorExplanations.c: Inventive speech does not preserve the witness’s own halting words.
